messages:
acme-cs: Hey team — after our plan cutover at 02:00 UTC our app saw a sudden spike in 429s against the dedicated pool. Started ~02:01. We moved 3 tenants in a batch.

maya-support: sorry to hear that — can you paste an example request id and the pool name? any chance you changed quotas during the cutover? :thinking_face:

acme-cs: pool is reserved-east-1-acme, request id 8f3a2b. We triggered the plan migration script which sets new quotas and calls /v1/admin/tenants/assign. No manual quota edits.

sam-oncall: looking at logs for reserved-east-1-acme now. I see rapid 429s starting 4832109880 for tenant acme-prod-1. Posting excerpt:```[2026-03-15T02:01:20Z] tenant=acme-prod-1 pool=reserved-east-1-acme code=RATE_LIMIT status=429 rate_key=tenant:acme-prod-1 units=0 allowed=0/60 window=60s event=throttle```

jules-sre: units=0 is suspicious — could be quota floor applied incorrectly on the new plan. Any chance the cutover set rampBurst=0 or rampWindow=0?

acme-cs: our migration manifest had "ramp_burst: 0" because we thought warmup would be handled elsewhere. Might that cause a hard zero allowance?

maya-support: that matches reproduction I ran locally — if ramp_burst is zero the quota calculator returns a zero initial bucket until the decay window accumulates tokens. For dedicated pools we have a separate warmup policy; a zero burst can effectively block traffic until autoscale/warmup kicks in.

sam-oncall: confirmed in control-plane trace:```
trace_id=tr-9a2
action=assign_quota tenant=acme-prod-1 new_plan=business-plus
compute_quota -> {base: 1200, ramp_burst: 0, cooldown: 300}
policy_applied -> dedicated_pool_warmup=false
```

jules-sre: keynotes: (1) dedicated pool expects non-zero ramp_burst or explicit warmup policy, (2) code path that translates plan -> quota had a unit conversion bug for cutover path that set effective units to 0 for first window, (3) autoscaler had ~90s delay due to warmup gating.

acme-cs: ouch. What's the immediate mitigation? Can we override ramp_burst per-tenant?

maya-support: yes — quick fix is to set an emergency quota override to give a temporary burst allowance:```
PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/acme-prod-1/quota
{ "override": { "burst_allowance": 300 } }
```

maya-support: I pushed that for acme-prod-1 and acme-prod-2 at 02:03 UTC. Can you validate traffic now? :white_check_mark:

acme-cs: traffic looks normal now, 429s subsided. Thanks.

sam-oncall: root cause plan: migration tool allowed ramp_burst=0. Follow-ups: add validation reject if dedicated pool + ramp_burst==0; add a safety fallback that treats 0 as unset (use default burst); instrument cutover path to emit quota diff events. I'll file a ticket.

jules-sre: also adding an alert for sudden drop-to-zero allowance in quota-metrics so we catch this earlier.

deploy-bot: CI job #4221 created ticket INF-5487 for migration-tool validation and INF-5488 for quota-alerting.

acme-cs: appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll re-run migration with corrected manifest and confirm.

maya-support: noted, closing this thread when you confirm final migration. If anything else pops up ping us in #support or @maya-support. :pray:
